definitions.gloss: full-time employment; full-time work; regular work
definitions.explanation: Working at a fixed schedule on a regular, full-time basis, as opposed to part-time or temporary work. Commonly used in job descriptions and employment contexts.

examples.japanese: {常勤|じょうきん}の{職員|しょくいん}を{募集|ぼしゅう}している。
{彼|かれ}は{常勤|じょうきん}{講師|こうし}として{働|はたら}いている。
examples.english: He works as a full-time lecturer.

examples.japanese: {非常勤|ひじょうきん}から{常勤|じょうきん}に{切|き}り{替|か}えたいと{思|おも}っているが、{空|あ}きがない。
examples.english: I want to switch from part-time to full-time, but there are no openings.

notes:
USAGE:
{常勤|じょうきん} combines {常|じょう} (always, regular) and {勤|きん} (work, service). It is most commonly used as a modifier before job titles. The antonym is {非常勤|ひじょうきん} (part-time, non-regular).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {常勤|じょうきん}{職員|しょくいん} (full-time employee)
- {常勤|じょうきん}{講師|こうし} (full-time lecturer)
- {常勤|じょうきん}{医師|いし} (full-time doctor)
- {非常勤|ひじょうきん} (part-time, non-regular)

SIMILAR WORDS:
フルタイム is the loanword equivalent used in casual contexts. {正社員|せいしゃいん} refers to a regular employee with full benefits, which often overlaps with {常勤|じょうきん} but emphasizes employment status rather than working hours.
